votes.why: The polished skeuomorphic UI/robot rendering and explicit infographic-like layout look like a deliberate stock/concept 3D render rather than a cinematic frame or real photograph.
The uniform studio-style lighting across the beveled interface makes it look like a static 3D mockup.

The biggest factor: this is a skeuomorphic web UI ("The Worst Job Application Ever" form with a Submit button, cursor and progress steps) with a stylized 3D look, which reads like a web or app demo rather than a photo, film frame or product render. The fine materials and lighting made (c) the runner-up.
the interactive job-application screen is itself the scene, with the 3D elements functioning as UI controls and game-like obstacles.

it's a polished but generic skeuomorphic 3D concept illustration (physical UI buttons, robot, progress bars) of the kind typical of stock/editorial 3D renders - too stylized and static for a film/game cinematic, and too rendered and composed to be a photo or an actual app/game screenshot.

the composition is an interactive game-like application screen, with the 3D pieces acting as interface controls around a visible cursor.

it is a flat software UI screenshot with typed labels, a cursor, and skeuomorphic low-budget app/web widgets rather than a photographed object or cinematic scene.

It's a flat web UI screen (a joke job-application form with a fake CAPTCHA) styled with skeuomorphic 3D-looking buttons and a paper texture. That reads as a web demo or low-budget app, not a photo or a cinematic render.

the perfectly front-on arrangement of sculpted UI controls reads like a standalone 3D illustration rather than a cinematic frame.

it's a clean, evenly lit studio-style still on a seamless paper background. It's not a photo of a real object, and it doesn't look like a cinematic film or game frame. It's too detailed and realistically shaded for a low-budget web or mobile 3D demo. It also looks AI-generated rather than hand-modeled.
The straight-on, product-mockup arrangement of the beveled 3D interface controls was the strongest cue.

the image is a stylized conceptual 3D composition: flat "UI element as physical object" props (submit pill, progress beads, cursor icon) arranged on a plain paper-like backdrop with clean, even studio lighting and smooth untextured surfaces, exactly the look of a high-end stock/concept 3D render. It lacks the environmental storytelling, characters, and cinematic framing of a film/game cinematic (b), and the physical impossibilities (floating smoke, cracked "button hole," typo "I am not a rabot") plus overly perfect materials rule out a real photograph (a). It's too polished for a low-budget app (d).
the straight-on, evenly sharp arrangement reads like a staged 3D mockup of a job application rather than a cinematic shot.

It is a polished, stylized 3D-looking UI concept: brushed-metal pieces, a frosted glass card, and a burnt "Submit" pill, all under clean studio lighting. That makes it look like an ordinary render or illustration, not a real photo or a film frame. Typos like "rabot" also hint that it may be AI-generated.
The app interface is staged as a static 3D product-style flat lay, with its buttons and cursor rendered as physical props.
The polished but generic studio-lit CGI materials and static conceptual-product composition look most like an ordinary high-end 3D render rather than a photograph or cinematic frame.
